meta_title: Compress Image to 50 KB Online, Free | Resize-It
meta_description: Reduce a JPG, PNG or WebP image to under 50 KB for online forms and uploads. Clean quality, measured results, no upload, no sign-up.
subtitle: Make a photo small enough for forms and portals that cap uploads at 50 KB, without turning it into a blurry mess. Runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

tool_workspace.description: Add one or more images; each is compressed to 50 KB or less.

requirements.intro: We compressed three 12-megapixel (3000 × 4000) phone photos to 50 KB with this tool:
requirements.notes_h3: Getting a good result at 50 KB
notes: Typical result: about 450–700 px wide. That is clear on screen and enough for an ID-style photo on a form.
50 KB is roughly 2.5 times the room of 20 KB, so the same photo keeps about 1.6–1.9 times the width.
Crop first. If the form wants a face or a signature, crop away everything else (use the image cropper): fewer pixels to store means more detail in the part that matters.
We count 1 KB as 1000 bytes, so a "20 KB" file from this page is at most 20,000 bytes. That is also under the limit for forms that count 1 KB as 1024 bytes.
PNG files are converted to JPEG (or to WebP if they have transparency), because PNG cannot be compressed this far without losing its format.
If a form also asks for exact pixel dimensions (for example 200 × 230 px), resize to those dimensions first with the image resizer, then compress here.

how_to.title: How to compress an image to 50 KB
how_to.step1_text: Select or drag in a JPG, PNG or WebP image. It is processed in your browser and never uploaded.
how_to.step2_text: "To a file size" is already selected with 50 KB. Change the number if your form asks for something else.
how_to.step3_text: Click Compress Image. The tool finds the best quality that fits; if needed it also makes the image smaller in pixels and tells you the new size.
how_to.step4_text: The file downloads automatically and is 50 KB or less, so it fits forms that count 1 KB as 1000 or as 1024 bytes.

items.q: How do I compress a photo to 50 KB?
items.a: Add the photo on this page and click Compress Image. The 50 KB limit is preset; the result downloads automatically.

items.q: Will the photo still look good?
items.a: Yes for screen use. The tool keeps JPEG quality at 60% or better and reduces the pixel size instead of making the picture blocky. In our tests a portrait stayed about 620–700 px wide.

items.q: Can I compress several photos to 50 KB at once?
items.a: Yes. Add several images; each is compressed to 50 KB or less and they download together as a ZIP.

items.q: What if my form needs both a size and a KB limit?
items.a: Resize to the required pixel size first with the image resizer, then compress to the KB limit here.
No. Everything runs on your device.
